d.d: Representing a loud noise or heavy impact.
d.x: The wind knocked the tree over last night. Bam! It nearly scared me to death.

d.d: Representing a sudden or abrupt occurrence.
d.x: She said she dumped him. Now — bam! — they're back together.

d.d: Alternative form of bamma (“an unstylish rural person; a hick”).
Nickname for Alabama: a state of the United States.
A child or baby, especially a representation in art of the infant Christ wrapped in swaddling clothes.
Any of the fast-growing grasses of the Bambusoideae subfamily, characterized by its woody, hollow, round, straight, jointed stem.
Wood of the bamboo plant as a material for building, furniture, etc.
A stick, rod, pole, or cane of bamboo, especially one used as a vessel for liquids, or as a tool for corporal punishment.
Made of the wood of the bamboo.
To flog with a bamboo cane.
To paint (furniture, etc.) to give it the appearance of bamboo.
third-person singular simple present indicative of bamboo
To con, defraud, trick, to make a fool of, to humbug or impose on someone.

d.x: He's completely bamboozled by the changes in the computer system.

d.d: simple past and past participle of bamboozle
Initialism of black, Asian, and minority ethnic.
